title: feat(desktop): Check and fix files reconciles the library with its folder
body:
Kaipu can now check the vault folder against the library and fix what disagrees, on demand. A banner in the Library and on Home offers **Check and fix files** when something does not match; the same action is in Settings → Files. The dialog lists every finding, **Fix all** runs one pass, and checking again finds nothing.

**Why.** PR #435 makes an in-app rename move the file, but nothing aligned the items that already existed. A read-only scan of the owner's vault (561 media files) found zero items whose file name matched their title: 527 carry old automatic titles (`Recording — 10/29/2026, 7:57:30 PM` over `recording-2026-10-30-00-57-30.mp4`). Files changed in Finder also drift from their records. Ticket: [NIW2-561](https://linear.app/niway/issue/NIW2-561/reconcile-the-library-with-its-folder-from-a-check-and-fix-files). Decision: ADR 0033 (`architecture/decisions/0033-the-library-reconciles-with-its-folder-on-demand.mdx`). **Stacked on #435** (base branch is #435's); merge #435 first.

## What changes for you

- **Fix all** does three things:
  - it renames files to their titles (Kaipu wins when the same item disagrees);
  - it replaces old automatic titles with the readable default name;
  - it adopts media that has no record, under its disk name.
- **Nothing is deleted.** A record or companion with no media (for example the old record of a file renamed in Finder) moves to `.kaipu/orphans/<run>/` with a manifest. Manual reassignment is [NIW2-589](https://linear.app/niway/issue/NIW2-589/orphaned-records-list-them-and-reassign-one-to-a-file-manually).
- **Ambiguous cases are listed, never touched:**
  - two items with one identity;
  - two media files on one stem (`Demo.mp4` + `Demo.PNG`);
  - companions shared between items;
  - unreadable records;
  - an unreadable orphan run;
  - uppercase extensions.
- **Maintenance mode.** Fix all does not start during a recording or export. While it runs, vault operations are refused with "Kaipu is fixing your files", not queued. Refused editor saves retry when it ends.
- **Fixes that apply everywhere, not only in Fix all:**
  - A corrupt sidecar is no longer overwritten with a new identity by listing, backfill, the editor, rename or delete; the item lists read-only.
  - A reload during a recording keeps its partial for recovery instead of leaking the vault lease; an export's partial is discarded.
  - Every placement of media into the vault (finalize, the stranded sweep, rename, GIF, screenshots, orphan moves, the save dialog) goes through one module, `safe-place.ts`. It never replaces an existing file and never deletes what it did not create.
  - An in-app rename onto a name that a file took at that moment now reports `kept-old-name` with the new reason `taken`, instead of overwriting.
  - Pasted images get the screenshot default name (in #435, `00abd0f5`).

## What to review

1. **`apps/kaipu-record/src/main/library/safe-place.ts`, the placement primitive and its threat model** (ADR 0033, "Placing a file"). It is guaranteed against our own concurrency, crashes, I/O errors, and files present or arriving before placement. It is not guaranteed against an external process replacing a path between two of our syscalls, because Node has no no-replace rename. Decide whether that boundary is acceptable.
2. **`apps/kaipu-record/src/main/library/vault-reconcile.ts`, the scan and the Fix all pipeline:**
   - the scan only reads;
   - committed-rename remnants are classified first;
   - the rename planner is rebuilt from a fresh scan;
   - orphan manifests are written before moves and replayed fail-closed.
3. **`apps/kaipu-record/src/main/library/vault-activity.ts` and its admission points.** Decide whether the inventory of entry points is complete. A missed writer could slip into a run.
4. **`apps/kaipu-record/src/main/recording/recording-hub.ts`, the take lifecycle.** Create, finalize, cursor write, cleanup and the lease release run as one path. Reload, crash and abort all end through it, once.
5. **The accepted limitations in ADR 0033:**
   - a rename in Finder makes a new item, with the old record in orphans;
   - a swap of two names in Finder swaps their metadata, as it does today;
   - a pre-existing item renamed in Finder keeps the Finder name.

**Safe to skim:** i18n en/es pairs, IPC/preload plumbing, the docs updates (`library-vault.mdx`, `ipc-contract.mdx`), and test fixtures.

## Proof

| Criterion | How to check it | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fix all aligns names, replaces old auto titles, adopts unknown files | `vault-reconcile*.test.ts`; manual steps 2–6 | Unit suite green. Manual: not verified by me (no Electron launch) |
| A second check finds nothing fixable | idempotence test on a fixture with every edge case (101 same titles, 6-chain, 2-cycle) | Unit suite green |
| Nothing is deleted; every payload survives any failure | fault injection at every read, copy, write, sync, close and rename of a Fix all run | Unit suite green |
| Vault work is refused during a fix; a fix waits or refuses during captures | `vault-activity` + hub tests | Unit suite green |
| Corrupt records are never overwritten | scan → fix → refresh → backfill byte-identical test | Unit suite green |

Adversarial review with GPT-6.1 Sol: 4 design rounds on the plan, then 7 code rounds; every finding came with a reproducing fixture. Round 7, under the threat model above, closed every earlier item and found one in-model blocker: a staging-file close error let the renderer's abort delete the only recording copy. It is fixed in `ac7c7b1b`, with a test that failed first. That last fix was not re-reviewed by Sol.

## Checks

- `bun run verify` → exit 0 (kaipu-record 3345+ tests at `2f026d2d`; the last two commits are verified by the push hook).
- Desktop Playwright E2E not run locally (ADR 0006).

## Manual verification

- [ ] Steps 1–8 below on a **copy** of the vault (macOS)
- [ ] Windows: rename with the file open in a player; Fix all on a vault on a USB/exFAT drive

## How to test it yourself

Use a **copy** of your vault; never point a QA build at the real one.

1. Copy `~/Movies/Kaipu Record` to `~/Movies/Kaipu Record QA`. Run `bun run dev` from this branch. In Settings → Files → Browse, pick the copy.
2. Open the Library.
   - Expect: a banner "N files in your folder don't match Kaipu".
3. Click **Check and fix** and read the table.
   - Expect: a **Now → After Fix all** table, for example `recording-2026-10-30-00-57-30` → `Kaipu Recording 2026-10-29 at 19.57.30`. Listed-only items appear in a second table, **File / Why it stays**.
   - Expect: old exports (`Recording — 9/14/2026, … (edited)`) show as `Kaipu Recording 2026-09-14 at 10.57.31 (edited)`, named after their source. They never show as `9 14 2026`.
4. Click **Fix all**.
   - Expect: progress with no Close button, then "Done. N items fixed, M files moved to the orphans folder."
5. Click **Check again**.
   - Expect: "Everything matches." or only listed items.
6. In Finder:
   - names match the Library titles;
   - tags and editor sessions still open;
   - `.kaipu/reconcile/` has a run log;
   - `.kaipu/orphans/<run>/manifest.json` exists if anything moved.
7. Rename a file in Finder, then run Fix all again.
   - Expect: it appears as a new item, and its old record is in `.kaipu/orphans/<new run>/`.
8. Start a recording and open the dialog.
   - Expect: it says a recording is in progress and stays dismissible.
   - Reload the window mid-recording (Cmd+R): the take is recovered on the next start, and Fix all is no longer "busy".
9. Point Settings → Files back to the real folder, or click Reset.

## What I did not verify

- **The app itself:** nothing ran in Electron. The banner, the dialog, refusals, editor retries and the reload paths are covered by unit tests only.
- **Windows, exFAT, SMB and HFS+:** locked files, NTFS links, directory sync, volumes without hard links and NFD names are all simulated with mocks.
- **Power-loss durability:** best effort (file and directory fsync), not proven.

## Follow-ups (tickets filed)

- recover a case-only rename's hidden temporary file;
- a whole-file copy per retry on volumes without hard links;
- the screenshot export's `writeFile` to a user path (pre-existing);
- case-only companion renames and `removePaths` by pathname.
